findings.source_passage: here be it said, that many tattooed savages sailing in Nantucket ships at last come to be converted into the churches
findings.source_locator: paragraph 7, after Ishmael's First Congregational claim
findings.why_it_matters: This authorial aside is a characteristic Melvillean digression that contextualizes the comic irony of Ishmael's claim; its absence flattens the narrator's wry, documentary voice that is central to the chapter's tone.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the aside as a parenthetical after the First Congregational line: '(here be it said, that many tattooed savages sailing in Nantucket ships at last come to be converted into the churches).'

findings.source_passage: we all belong to that; only some of us cherish some queer crotchets no ways touching the grand belief; in _that_ we all join hands
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops the italicized emphasis on 'that' ('in _that_ we all join hands'), which is rhetorically deliberate—the stress carries the rhetorical climax of Ishmael's argument. Also omits the prefatory 'we all belong to that,' weakening the anaphoric force.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'we all belong to that; only some of us…in _that_ we all join hands' with the italics intact.

findings.source_passage: jumped upon the bulwarks, from thence into the bows of one of the whale-boats hanging to the side; and then bracing his left knee, and poising his harpoon
findings.why_it_matters: The precise kinetic choreography—bulwarks, then bows, hanging to the side—establishes Queequeg's seamless physical competence; collapsing it to 'leaped to a boat in the davits' loses both the specificity and the rhythmic accumulation that makes the moment vivid.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-step movement: bulwarks first, then into the bows of a hanging whale-boat, before the knee-bracing and poising.

findings.thou thyself, as I myself, hast seen man: source_locator": "Bildad's rejoinder, paragraph after Nat Swaine anecdote
findings.why_it_matters: The draft strips 'as I myself,' 'thou knowest, Peleg, what it is to have the fear of death,' 'in this ungodly guise,' and 'Thou beliest thine own heart, Peleg'—losing the archaic rhythmic intensity of Bildad's counter-argument and his personal appeal, which gives Peleg's response its dramatic weight.
findings.suggested_fix: Expand Bildad's speech to include 'thou knowest, Peleg, what it is to have the fear of death; how, then, can'st thou prate in this ungodly guise. Thou beliest thine own heart, Peleg.'

findings.source_passage: He got so frightened about his plaguy soul, that he shrinked and sheered away from whales, for fear of after-claps, in case he got stove and went to Davy Jones.
findings.why_it_matters: 'Plaguy soul,' 'shrinked and sheered,' and 'got stove and went to Davy Jones' are period-specific, voice-marking idioms; the draft substitutes a bare paraphrase 'sheered from whales for fear of after-claps,' losing the comic accumulation.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'so frightened about his plaguy soul, that he shrinked and sheered away from whales…in case he got stove and went to Davy Jones.'

summary: No high-severity signature losses; two medium findings (the narrator's aside on tattooed sailors converting, and the loss of rhetorical italics in Ishmael's 'Catholic Church' speech) represent meaningful voice-flattening but do not individually or collectively meet the regeneration threshold.
